chitchat: No, I'll not, and you're very good to keep asking.
It isn't a secret. It's just not a sentence.
You'll get it, or you'll not, and either is all right.
description: An old woman sitting on the end of a bench near the worn patch of floor, not at the front and not facing anywhere in particular. She's mending a sleeve. She's extremely pleased to see you and makes no attempt to hide it, and at no point does she ask you a single question about yourself.

bye.text:
"Mind how you go."

They lift a hand off the blanket and let it drop again.

options.label: What am I supposed to do here?

hall.text:
"People sit in it."

A pause you could drive a truck through.

"There's a bit at the end where somebody stands, if they have got something. Mostly nobody has. It's very restful. You're welcome to sit in it whenever you like."

Behind her, at the far end of the hall, four people who haven't spoken to each other get up at the same moment and go out by different doors. She doesn't turn round.

options.label: What am I supposed to do here?

leave.text:
"Out."

She threads the needle, which at her age takes a moment and which she doesn't hurry.

"I'm not being difficult. We don't say the place. Not to you, not to Stannard, not much to each other. The machine kept every record there has ever been and the one place it never reached was the inside of a head, and a thing that's said out loud stops being in there."

"So we're going out. And we're taking a very long time over it, and we're getting it right."

me.text:
"Whatever you would have done anyway."

She holds the sleeve up to the light, decides against it, and starts again.

"Eat with everybody. Wash up your own bowl. If somebody is carrying something heavy, take an end. If a door doesn't open for you, don't stand there arguing with it, there's nobody to argue with."

"And don't tell anybody in here what you used to be. Not because we would mind. Because you'll want to, badly, for about a fortnight, and then one morning you'll not, and that morning is worth having."

root.first:
"Oh, good." She puts the sleeve down. "I did wonder how long. Sit, sit. Nobody is doing anything."

"Have you come far?"

options.label: What am I supposed to do here?

text_by_relation.close: "Ah." She doesn't look up from the sleeve, and moves along the bench, and carries on.
text_by_relation.familiar: "There you are." She makes room she didn't need to make.
text_by_relation.known: "You're still here." She sounds delighted about it.

options.label: What am I supposed to do here?

what.text:
"It's where we live."

She waits, quite comfortably, to see whether you'll accept that. When you do not, she smiles at the sleeve.

"You want me to say a bigger word. I have got one. Everybody in here has got one. The trouble with the bigger word is that once I say it, that's what you'll have come here and found, and you'll stop looking, and what you found will be a word."

"So. It's where we live. Ask me again in a year."

name: Thankful Sedge
